note: A kind of reader, not a person. Every name, date and line here is fictional; nobody has been sent this page. The personal part (a reader's name) would travel only in the link's fragment, which the browser never sends.
title: For a project manager
reader: a delivery lead who plans and runs work across several teams
judges: Could my team run this, and where does it break?
why_you: You plan work for teams that have to deliver. If this rhythm and this way of deciding would not survive your planning cycle, you will say where it breaks.

ask.by_note: an example date: nothing has been sent

gets: your name in the acknowledgements, if you want it there
the first edition when it ships
a reply to every comment, and a page showing what your comments changed

chapters.why: the rhythm of the work, every hour
how decisions are asked for and signed

chapters_note: Chapters proposed by the storyteller (team/storyteller/review-questions.md), a proposal until the editor rules on the length per page; the 'short of time' chapter is developer@'s proposal.

questions.q: Could you run a team this way? What would you need that is not here?
How would you know, from what the team leaves behind, that the work was on track?
Where would this rhythm clash with the way your teams already plan?
What would you report upward from it?
How are decisions asked for and made here? Is that clear?
What would happen in this process if the decision-maker were away for a day?
Which part would you adopt in your own governance?

short_note: the one chapter to read when short of time: a proposal by developer@ from synthetic@'s runs, for the editor to keep or change
